subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw use when active exec-backed providers fail under a service supervisor?
rationale: Current code intentionally fails closed for active SecretRefs at startup, but supervisor restarts can amplify side-effecting credential-provider calls; choosing retry, degraded boot, or circuit-break behavior changes security and operator semantics.

options.title: Define generic guarded startup policy
options.body: Adopt a bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry/degraded-mode policy with clear operator diagnostics and tests for exec failures without adding 1Password-specific behavior.

options.title: Document supervisor mitigation only
options.body: Keep fail-fast startup semantics and document launchd/systemd restart limits plus batchable resolver patterns as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Add configurable retry surface
options.body: Introduce a new `secrets` retry/circuit-breaker config, accepting the compatibility and schema surface cost with doctor/docs/tests.

recommendation.title: Define generic guarded startup policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry/degraded-mode policy with clear operator diagnostics and tests for exec failures without adding 1Password-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The deepest concrete provenance for the SecretRef provider and eager runtime snapshot behavior points to this owner trail.
